# piknit

**A way to embed the [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works) coding
agent in R.** Drive a live agent from R with a small scripting API —
[`pi_run()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_run.md)
for one turn,
[`pi_session()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_session.md)
for a memory-keeping multi-turn session — or drop it straight into R
Markdown / Quarto through knitr engines that run a *live* agent (and
fail-loud shell commands) at render time, weaving the agent’s real
replies and command output into the document. **Rendering becomes an
integration test**: a stale claim or a broken command fails the build.
Same idea as `leanknit` and `duckknit`, pointed at an agent.

Two ways to use it:

- **As an R binding** —
  [`pi_run()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_run.md)
  /
  [`pi_session()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_session.md)
  call a Pi agent from any R script, app, or pipeline; the agent (with
  its tools and extensions) becomes a function you call and whose reply
  you keep.
- **As literate engines** — ```` ```{pi} ```` and ```` ```{pish} ````
  chunks put a live agent and fail-loud commands into a rendered
  document.

## Install

``` r

# remotes::install_github("sounkou-bioinfo/piknit")
library(piknit)
```

Needs the `pi` CLI on the `PATH`. Set defaults with
`options(piknit.model=, piknit.provider=)` or the `PIKNIT_PI` env var.

## Call the agent from R

The agent is a function you call; its reply is a character vector you
keep — run live when this README renders:

``` r

reply <- pi_run("In one sentence, what is a coding agent?")
reply
```

``` R
A coding agent is an AI system that helps you write, edit, run, and manage code by interacting with files, tools, and tests—like this assistant.
```

Point it at an extension (`extension = "path/to/index.ts"`) to give the
agent tools. That is the whole embedding:
[`pi_run()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_run.md)
is one turn,
[`pi_session()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_session.md)
is a memory-keeping conversation, and the knitr engines below are just
these calls wired into a render.

## The `pi` engine — the chunk body is the prompt

Write a prompt in a ```` ```{pi} ```` chunk; at render time a live agent
turn runs and its reply is woven in under the exact command used. A
small, fast model (`gpt-5.3-codex-spark` by default) keeps a live turn
to seconds.

```` R
```{pi}
In one sentence, what is literate programming?
```
````

``` sh
pi --model gpt-5.3-codex-spark -p \
  "In one sentence, what is literate programming?"
```

> Literate programming is a style where you write code as part of a
> human-readable document (with explanations) and then weave it into
> executable code.

## The `pish` engine — fail-loud shell

Run a command; a non-zero exit **stops the render** (never bakes a
failure as an answer), and JSON output is fenced for highlighting.

```` R
```{pish}
node --version
```
````

## Set the project root

pi treats its working directory as the **project root** — what scopes
the agent’s file tools and where relative extension / skill / manifest
paths resolve. Point any call at a root with `dir`:

``` r

pi_run(
  "Count variants by consequence in examples/variant-counts/manifest.json.",
  dir = "~/pi-bio-agent",
  extension = "extensions/pi-coding-agent/index.ts"
)
```

## Stream the response

Because pi’s `--mode rpc` emits JSON events as they happen,
[`pi_stream()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_stream.md)
delivers the reply incrementally — assistant text as deltas, every event
to a callback — ending on pi’s `agent_end`:

``` r

pi_stream("Explain content-addressed storage in two sentences.")          # prints as it is typed
pi_stream("...", on_event = function(ev) if (ev$type == "turn_end") message("done"))
```

## A persistent session across chunks

[`pi_session()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_session.md)
gives successive turns shared conversation memory (via a stable
`--session-id`) without holding a long-lived process, so an earlier
chunk’s result is in scope later:

``` r

s <- pi_session(dir = "~/pi-bio-agent", extension = "extensions/pi-coding-agent/index.ts")
s$ask("Load examples/variant-counts/manifest.json and count variants by consequence.")
s$ask("Now express the same counts as percentages.")  # remembers the table above
```

## Why

Docs that *run* don’t drift. Pointing the render at a live agent turns a
README, a vignette, or a tutorial into a real end-to-end test of the
agent, its tools, and the claims you make about them — the discipline
that caught real bugs while building
[pi-bio-agent](https://github.com/sounkou-bioinfo/pi-bio-agent),
piknit’s first user.

# Package index

## Embed the agent in R

Drive a live Pi coding agent from R — one turn, a streaming turn, or a
session.

- [`pi_run()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_run.md)
  : Run one turn of a live Pi agent
- [`pi_stream()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_stream.md)
  : Stream a live Pi agent turn as it happens
- [`pi_session()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_session.md)
  : Open a persistent Pi agent session

## The reply object

The classed value an agent turn returns.

- [`print(`*`<pi_reply>`*`)`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_reply.md)
  [`as.character(`*`<pi_reply>`*`)`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/pi_reply.md)
  : The reply from a Pi agent turn

## knitr engines

Run a live agent (and fail-loud commands) inside a rendered document.

- [`register_engines()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/register_engines.md)
  : Register piknit's knitr engines

## Utilities

- [`wrap_prompt()`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/wrap_prompt.md)
  : Wrap a prompt onto short, runnable shell-string lines

## Package

- [`piknit`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/piknit-package.md)
  [`piknit-package`](https://sounkou-bioinfo.github.io/piknit/reference/piknit-package.md)
  : piknit: embed the Pi coding agent in R
